intentComment: //local-deploy: "Story 003 — local Anvil deployment orchestration". `dev` itself carries no own doc-comment; it is the composite one-shot boot of the local anvil chain (clean, anvil, DeployMocks, yield sim, address extraction, TS codegen, API server).

base.command: npm run clean:local && npm run start:anvil & sleep 3 && LOCAL_PROMO_KENDU=true npm run deploy:local && ./simulate-yield.sh && npm run extract:addresses && npm run generate:ts-anvil && npm run serve

noVariantsNote: There are NO dev:preview / dev:dry / dev:broadcast siblings. `dev` is the only key in its stem. It is inherently a broadcasting key (forge --broadcast) but only against http://localhost:8545.

shellDecomposition.note: `&` binds looser than `&&`, so the line is TWO pipelines, not one.

pipelineA_background.text: npm run clean:local && npm run start:anvil
pipelineA_background.effect: wipes local state, then starts a long-lived anvil (never exits)

pipelineB_foreground.text: sleep 3 && LOCAL_PROMO_KENDU=true npm run deploy:local && ./simulate-yield.sh && npm run extract:addresses && npm run generate:ts-anvil && npm run serve

steps.role: fixed-duration readiness proxy for anvil; no health probe

steps.cmd: npm run clean:local && forge script script/DeployMocks.s.sol:DeployMocks --rpc-url http://localhost:8545 --broadcast --slow --gas-estimate-multiplier 300
steps.role: the sole forge target; note it re-runs clean:local a SECOND time
cast send MockDola.mint(MockAutoDOLA, 2300e18) using the well-known anvil key 0xac09…ff80
express API on :3001-ish serving /contracts, /progress, /health; blocks forever

raceCharacterisation: clean:local runs CONCURRENTLY with pipeline B, not before it. Ordering between the background wipe and the foreground `sleep 3` is unsynchronised. In practice the wipe wins (rm is fast, sleep is 3s), but nothing enforces it.

deploy:local's own leading `npm run clean:local` re-runs the wipe a second time, at a point where anvil is already up. That second wipe includes `rm -rf ~/.foundry/anvil/tmp/*` — it deletes anvil scratch state from under the RUNNING anvil that pipeline A just started, and it deletes broadcast/*/31337 that the immediately following forge run is about to write.

Anvil readiness is asserted only by `sleep 3` — no `cast block-number` / port poll. On a cold machine (anvil binary paging in, WSL2 under load) 3s can be short; DeployMocks then fails on its first RPC call with a connection error and the chain aborts before any `&&` successor runs, leaving a live orphan anvil from pipeline A.

STALE-ANVIL FAILURE MODE (the dangerous one): if an anvil is ALREADY listening on 8545, pipeline A's `anvil --port 8545` fails to bind and dies, but `sleep 3` in pipeline B does not care. deploy:local then broadcasts DeployMocks onto the PRE-EXISTING chain — which may already hold a prior deployment. The run appears to succeed, but nonces, addresses and wiring are layered onto stale state, and progress.31337.json is rewritten as if it were a fresh chain. There is no `require(block.chainid == 31337)` genesis-freshness assert in DeployMocks, so nothing catches it.
Because pipeline A is backgrounded, its exit status is discarded; `npm run dev` reports success/failure only for pipeline B.
`npm run serve` never returns, so Ctrl-C kills the foreground server but leaves the background anvil running — which is precisely the stale-anvil precondition for the NEXT `npm run dev`.

forgeTarget.broadcastKey: vm.envUint("ANVIL_PRIVATE_KEY") at DeployMocks.s.sol:387 — NOT set by the `dev` key or by any .envrc present in the submodule; documented only in the project CLAUDE.md:476 (0xac0974bec…ff80, anvil account 0). Absent env => the whole chain aborts at step 2.

envReads.name: LOCAL_PROMO_KENDU
envReads.note: The delta added this to `dev` explicitly, pinning the ARMED leg. Since the vm.envOr default is already true, setting it in `dev` is a no-op today — but it makes the DORMANT leg unreachable from `dev` without editing package.json.
